source.title: Just How Flexible are Neural Networks in Practice?
source.authors: Ravid Shwartz-Ziv; Micah Goldblum; Arpit Bansal; C. Bruss; Yann LeCun; Andrew Gordon Wilson

page_placements.theme: Generalization diagnostics provide information beyond training fit

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, including appendices.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures perfect-fitting capacity with EMC across semantic and random labels and altered inputs, a different measure aimed at the same fitting question.
record.gate_note: The paper reports EMC, the largest sample size achieving perfect training accuracy. It does not report test error at chance, training-time ratios, a sweep over corrupted-label fractions, or a real-labels-first training trajectory. Appendix figure results are not numerically recoverable from the supplied text. Related-work statements about prior studies are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: EMC directly measures the largest sampled training set fitted with 100% training accuracy. It therefore tests random-label and unstructured-input fitting, and the effect of weight decay on fitting, although it does not establish the complete original claims.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: practical fitting capacity depends on data, architecture, optimization, and regularization, and parameter count alone does not determine it. The authors also emphasize CNN parameter efficiency even with random labels and the relationship between semantic-versus-random fitting capacity and generalization.
record.recipe_differences: Measures maximum sample count achieving perfect training accuracy (EMC), rather than directly testing the original studies' training-error and test-error outcomes; varies architecture, inputs, labels, and training choices.
record.method_sensitivity: Architecture and input structure change EMC: CNN capacity falls when spatial structure is broken, MLP capacity is described as unchanged, and Gaussian noise increases capacity for both. Label type also changes capacity.

fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Label smoothing can reduce practical perfect-fitting capacity, including on randomly labeled data.

fits_no_version.finding: The semantic-versus-random-label EMC advantage correlates inversely with generalization gap: Pearson correlations are −0.9281 for CNNs and −0.869 for MLPs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A network's relative capacity for semantic versus random labels predicts its generalization gap.

record.problems: Most results relevant here are shown only in figures without recoverable values in the supplied text. EMC measures the largest perfectly fit sample size and does not directly give test error or the outcome for a specified dataset size. The authors also state that only a limited number of settings were explored for each factor.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant result rows were omitted. Other optimizer and architecture comparisons do not directly measure versions beyond the EMC/input/regularizer results recorded above.

untested.parts: Chance-level test error and fitting with hyperparameters unchanged from true-label training are not established. Learning rate and batch size are tuned for each setup.
Training-time ratios and convergence changes across corrupted-label fractions.
Independently permuted pixels and perfect fitting of an identical specified full dataset across all input transformations.
A corruption-fraction sweep jointly measuring perfect training fit and steadily worsening test error.
Dropout, data augmentation, and whether removing explicit regularization preserves good true-label generalization. Augmentation is omitted throughout rather than experimentally compared.
The temporal order of learning shared patterns and memorizing noise. Separate semantic-label and random-label capacities do not establish learning order.

missing.what: Random-label EMC for ViTs and the architecture comparison showing CNNs more parameter-efficient than both ViTs and MLPs. These extend the tested system coverage beyond R1 and R2; exact curve values cannot be recovered.
The CIFAR-100 class-count experiment reports that random-label fitting capacity increases as the number of classes increases, whereas semantic-label capacity decreases.
Random-label fitting across optimizers: the semantic-label capacity advantage of SGD and Shampoo disappears with random labels. This is an endpoint capacity comparison, not a training-time test.

record.verdict_notes: Unavailable numerical figure values do not erase explicit qualitative results or EMC's definition as perfect training accuracy. Capacity reductions qualify dataset-size scope; they do not establish a general inability to memorize random labels. No verdict treats missing test-error or timing measurements as contrary evidence.

versions.untested_parts: Does not report test error at chance or test fitting under unchanged hyperparameters as a fixed training-set outcome; reports EMC instead.
Training-time ratios and convergence slowdown as corrupted-label fraction rises are not measured.
Reports EMC for random inputs and fixed-permutation inputs, not an explicit zero-error result on a specified full training set; independently permuted pixels are not separately described.
No sweep over fractions of randomly corrupted labels or corresponding test-error results.
Tests weight decay and label smoothing on EMC with random labels; does not test dropout, data augmentation, or whether removing regularizers harms generalization on true labels.
Does not compare learning of real and random labels over training time.

tranche.reason: The EMC search measures maximum perfectly fitted sample count under converged training, a different method addressing practical random-label and unstructured-input fitting.

source_check.notes: Exact EMC values cannot be recovered from the supplied text; Figure 2 has conflicting architecture assignments. Learning rate and batch size are tuned per setup, augmentation is omitted, and these results do not establish unchanged hyperparameters, chance test performance, independent permutations or every component of V5.

statements.correction: Fixed-size MLPs and CNNs have lower EMC for random than semantic labels. Above measured EMC, perfect fitting fails after repeated converged runs. This supports limits_scope for dataset size; training accuracy beyond EMC is not numerically reported.
statements.problem: The capacity finding is accurate, but the challenges label overstates this study's evidence: failure of perfect fitting beyond EMC does not establish absent or negligible random-label learning.
